claims.text: A partially recrystallized heterogeneous grain structure can simultaneously increase yield strength and tensile ductility in an FCC-based multi-principal element alloy.
Lowering the stacking-fault energy to a room-temperature twinning-active range is a necessary component of the proposed strategy.
The initial coarse-grained FCC MPEA has low room-temperature ductility because its SFE is high or it lacks strain-hardening mechanisms.
Cold rolling by 60–80% introduces a high dislocation density and stored energy.
Short annealing below the full-recrystallization condition produces fine recrystallized grains while retaining coarse deformed grains.
Adding trace carbon or nitrogen, or otherwise adjusting composition, lowers SFE and activates deformation twinning at room temperature.
An annealing range of 800–900 °C is suitable for retaining a heterogeneous grain structure in CrCoNi systems.
The resulting microstructure contains nanometer-to-micrometer recrystallized grains together with coarse, heavily deformed grains.
Deformation twins and/or transformation-induced phases form dynamically during tensile deformation of the heterogeneous structure.
The fine recrystallized grains raise yield strength through Hall–Petch strengthening.
Interfaces between coarse and fine grains generate geometrically necessary dislocations and back stresses during deformation.
Back-stress hardening elevates flow stress and delays necking.
Coarse deformed grains act as strain-hardening reservoirs and accommodate large plastic strains.
Deformation twinning or TRIP supplies additional strain-hardening capacity.
The combined mechanisms prevent premature shear localization that otherwise causes brittleness in homogeneous or conventionally fine-grained MPEAs.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength exceeding 1000 MPa.
The processed alloy will retain at least 20–25% uniform tensile elongation.
The processed alloy will have total tensile elongation greater than 30%.
MPEAs with yield strength above 1000 MPa conventionally have less than 10% ductility.

The hypothesis is falsified if the heterogeneous sample fails to improve both yield strength and uniform elongation over the fully recrystallized ultrafine-grained control, including if it exceeds 1000 MPa but has less than 10% uniform elongation.

contradictions.description: The initial-state description characterizes as-cast or homogenized FCC MPEAs as having low room-temperature ductility, whereas the baseline states that standard arc-melted and homogenized MPEAs typically exhibit 40–50% ductility.
